summary: Romantic single-page Valentine proposal website with playful interactive buttons (including an evasive reject/decline button), celebratory fireworks on acceptance, a final photo/message screen, and a personalized first page header name (“EMAN”) in a lovely font.

existing_features.title: Create a single-page Valentine proposal experience that asks the user’s wife to be the user’s Valentine, with clearly separated phases: (1) proposal prompt screen, (2) acceptance celebration (fireworks), (3) final screen with a cute photo and the message “Much love.”

On the proposal prompt screen, implement two prominent buttons: a playful “YES” button and a decline button. The “YES” button must be clickable and visually inviting (e.g., animated/pulsing/hover feedback) without breaking accessibility.

Implement the decline button behavior so it actively avoids being clicked: each time the user attempts to click it, it moves to a new position anywhere within the visible viewport bounds and changes its label text each time (a different message per attempt). Ensure the button never renders off-screen or under fixed UI elements.

When the user clicks “YES”, transition immediately to a celebratory fireworks animation, then automatically transition to the final screen after the celebration completes (with a short, pleasant duration).

Final screen: display a cute photo (provided as a static asset) and the message “Much love.” Ensure the layout is responsive for mobile and desktop, and the image is displayed with appropriate scaling/cropping (no distortion).

Apply a cohesive romantic visual theme across the entire single-page experience (typography, color palette, background, button styling, spacing). Choose a distinct style that fits a Valentine proposal and keep it consistent across all states.
Add the required generated image(s) to the frontend as static assets under frontend/public/assets/generated and use them directly from the frontend (no backend image serving).

On the first/proposal page, display the name "EMAN" at the top of the screen with a lovely, romantic font style that matches the existing theme, without breaking the current layout of the proposal prompt and buttons.

On the proposal screen, display a clearly labeled "NO" button positioned side-by-side with the "YES!" button (same row on desktop; may wrap/stack responsively on small screens) before any evasive movement occurs.

When the user tries to interact with the NO button (click, hover, or keyboard focus), it must move to a new position within the visible viewport/container bounds and change its label text each time (use English phrases), ensuring it never renders off-screen or under fixed UI elements.
